entries.title: You can now generate, preview, and edit documents, PDFs, presentations, spreadsheets, and more directly in Gemini.
entries.summary: Generate, edit, and preview PDFs or Docs directly in Gemini. Use the new full-screen editor to refine your files today. See what's new in Gemini.
entries.content:
We’re introducing new ways to create and refine documents, PDFs, presentations, spreadsheets, code, and more in the Gemini app.

You can now generate, preview, and edit files right within your chat — expand to full screen to type edits directly, highlight text to ask questions, or have Gemini refine your files. PDF preview and editing is supported on both the web and mobile, while all other formats (Google Docs, Google Sheets, slide decks, Markdown files, TXT files, and code) are supported on the web only.

As shown in the video below, you can now ask Gemini to create a PDF study guide from your uploaded handwritten lecture notes and then you can easily manually edit, highlight specific sections to have Gemini make edits to text or visuals, and even ask further questions.

These capabilities are now available to all users in all languages where Gemini app is available.

entries.title: Colorado students joined a Google hackathon to tackle energy grid challenges.
entries.summary: Students at the Google Colorado Impact Hackathon built AI tools like SolarSnap to modernize the energy grid. See the winning innovations here.
entries.content:
We held the second annual Colorado Impact Hackathon at our Boulder offices, in partnership with CU Boulder and the Colorado Energy Office.

Participating students tackled a crucial challenge: How can we create a clean, secure, and resilient electric grid in Colorado? The winning projects addressed this head on:

  • First place: SolarSnap, an AI app that helps homeowners find the ideal setup for solar panels using their phone’s camera
  • Second place: Grid Watch, an AI-managed battery network designed to keep power on during wildfire shutoffs while reducing electricity costs.
  • Third place: Grid Guard, providing predictive capabilities for targeted grid hardening

At the event, Colorado Attorney General Phil Weiser and CU Boulder Vice Chancellor for Sustainability Andrew Mayock highlighted the importance of bold innovation to shape Colorado’s clean energy future.

From mitigating wildfire risks to tackling energy backlogs, events like these demonstrate how collaboration between students, public leaders, and technologists can drive meaningful change for Colorado.

entries.title: Gemini Notebook makes hundreds of textbooks available to help students learn even more.
entries.summary: Add textbooks from OpenStax and S Chand to Google Gemini Notebook. Generate custom study guides and quizzes now. See the available catalog.
entries.content:
Last month, we introduced Expert Intelligence, a cross-Google initiative that helps you engage with your trusted sources through Google AI products. While you can already add eligible ebooks purchased from Google Play Books, today we’re expanding that experience so students can easily add materials for their courses.

Students can now access hundreds of textbooks from providers in the U.S. and India including OpenStax, Open Textbook Library, and S Chand Publishing, right in Gemini Notebook at no charge. Once you add a textbook, every answer is grounded directly in the textbook, with inline citations and direct links back to the original source. Gemini Notebook also lets you transform textbook content into tailored study guides, practice quizzes, flashcards, and more.

To explore and add these textbooks, select “Add sources” within your notebook and select “Textbooks” to see the available catalog.

entries.title: Celebrate Halloween with these tricks in Google Photos.
entries.summary: Use Ask Photos to find past costumes and edit spooky backgrounds in Google Photos. Try these festive tricks to perfect your Halloween snaps today.
entries.content:
Halloween is all about pumpkin patches, clever costumes, and unforgettable spooky nights. Don’t let those memories just sit in your library. Bring them to life with these Google Photos tips and tricks:

  • React to photos in shared albums with any emoji to truly match the moment. 🎃🧟🦇🍬🧛
  • Want to avoid a costume repeat? Use Ask Photos 1 to search, “What costumes have I worn on Halloween?” and summon memories instantly.
  • Edit with Ask Photos 2 to swap a background for a more spooky scene, like a graveyard or haunted house. You can also add eerie lighting, remove photobombers, and more — all you have to do is ask.
  • Try editing your images with Moods 3 , like “Night lights” for an evening aesthetic perfect for late night Halloween snaps.
  • Create a custom collage of your favorite costumes using templates or customized borders with the color of your choice.

Try these tricks and more in the Google Photos app today!

entries.title: Equipping healthcare professionals with practical AI skills
entries.summary: Introduction of the Google AI for Healthcare Professionals Certificate
entries.content:
As I’ve traveled around the world this year, I’ve heard loud and clear from healthcare professionals how much need there is for a thoughtful but practical educational resource on AI, made specifically for healthcare. Today, we're announcing the Google AI for Healthcare Professionals Certificate, a new program designed to teach responsible, practical ways to use AI in day-to-day work. Built to fit busy schedules, the program offers flexible, self-paced lessons that focus on non-clinical administrative tasks. It is designed to be completed in less than five hours and to keep patients’ safety and privacy front and center.

Having spent my career in medicine, I know that people in healthcare are driven by a shared purpose to care for others, support families, and make a meaningful difference in their communities. Technology offers a real opportunity to support that purpose. Across disciplines, care teams are navigating how AI can shoulder administrative tasks and create more time for what matters most: patients.

Reclaiming that time has never been more urgent. A National Nursing Workforce Survey found that nearly one in three registered nurses planned to leave or retire due to unsustainable workloads. Emerging technologies are poised to ease these pressures, but nine out of 10 doctors say they want dedicated training in how to use AI effectively. Regardless of your role in healthcare, navigating AI tools shouldn’t be something you have to figure out on your own. The Google AI for Healthcare Professionals Certificate offers an opportunity to build these skills, while earning up to 5.0 AMA PRA Category 1 Credits™.

Healthcare organizations are already putting the training into practice. NYU Grossman School of Medicine, University of Alabama at Birmingham, and Touro University are offering it to their faculty, residents, and medical students. Additionally, leading nursing institutions, including Purdue University School of Nursing, are offering the certificate as part of their healthcare professional training.

Clinical and medical education professionals who reviewed the curriculum also emphasize the importance of practical AI literacy.

Built by healthcare professionals for healthcare professionals

Developed by clinicians at Google — with backgrounds spanning internal medicine, pediatrics, critical care medicine, emergency medicine, and public health — the curriculum draws on draft versions of the Association of American Medical Colleges (AAMC) Artificial Intelligence Competencies Across the Learning Curriculum (which was under development at the time of the initial course design, but reflected the overall direction of the final competencies).

Across four courses, learners will explore high-impact ways to integrate AI into their daily routines.

  • Build foundational skills: Spot practical ways to use AI and confidently evaluate outputs, keeping clinical judgement, safety, and privacy at the forefront.
  • Strengthen patient communication: Translate complex medical concepts into clear, patient-friendly audio and visual guides, helping patients better understand and manage their care.
  • Optimize day-to-day administrative tasks: Streamline non-clinical work — like scheduling or reviewing dense email threads — and use natural language to build helpful tools without coding.
  • Accelerate lifelong learning: Digest complex clinical studies, organize presentations, and sharpen preparation for exams and certifications.

Designed to give time back to patient care

Continuing education is non-negotiable in healthcare, and this course is one step in supporting AI education for healthcare professionals. By streamlining the routine tasks that pull you away from the bedside, our goal is simple: to give you back the time, the focus, and the joy of caring for your patients.

Learn more and register today at grow.google/healthcare.

entries.title: How to use Gemini to update your resume
entries.summary: Turn raw notes into high-impact, ATS-friendly resume bullets using Gemini. Follow these four steps to polish your professional profile. Get the details.
entries.content:
In four simple steps:

1. Open Gemini and ramble at it about all your past roles.

2. Add this prompt: “Act as a professional resume writer. Use my raw, unedited notes about my past work and turn it into four high-impact resume bullets for a _______ role. Start each bullet with a strong action verb. Keep the tone executive, clear, and ATS-friendly."

3. Chat back and forth to adjust details, tone, and focus.

4. Copy and paste it into your resume when it’s done.

entries.title: How Gemini is helping students and teachers in the classroom
entries.summary: A teacher crouching next to a student seated at a desk as they talk. In front of the student are papers and a laptop.
entries.content:
Technology best serves education when it creates space for inspiring teaching and deeper learning. To better understand how AI tools perform in everyday educational settings, we’ve spent the past year working alongside educators and researchers in classrooms across the UK and Italy.

From testing one-on-one AI math tutoring to analyzing thousands of hours of classroom collaboration, today we’re sharing new research findings that demonstrate the impact of this technology on the process of teaching and learning. Together, the results show that AI tutoring using Gemini capabilities can deliver support on par with human tutors for UK students when used responsibly with human oversight, while Gemini itself can foster more collaborative classrooms and support teacher wellbeing in Italy.

UK: Scaling reliable, effective math tutoring

To truly understand how student learning is being shaped, we need to study it over time across diverse classroom settings. We previously ran an exploratory study with Eedi, which found that AI tutoring could operate effectively in real classrooms. The study tested an AI tutor combining Gemini capabilities with Eedi's study platform, designed to identify a student’s specific mistake and guide them to fix it themselves.

This year, we set out to better understand Gemini's pedagogical capabilities and the nuances of student learning in structured mathematics lessons. We conducted a 10-week randomized controlled trial (RCT) with over 1,100 students (ages 12-15) in the UK to measure their learning gains in math through sessions on Eedi’s school platform. Educators were actively involved at every stage of the study — with teachers monitoring student progress and providing hands-on support in the classroom, and tutors guiding students one-on-one through the platform.

Whenever a student answered a question incorrectly, they received one of three types of support: a static hint, help from a human tutor, or interactive AI tutoring combining Eedi’s pedagogical resources with Gemini. To ensure teaching quality, human experts reviewed every AI response in real time before it reached a student. While test scores aren’t the only measure of learning outcomes, over the course of the trial, we tracked their progress across regular assignments in the Eedi platform, intermediate quizzes, and independent STAR standardized tests.

This trial revealed major leaps in model quality and student performance. Compared to last year’s study, Gemini’s pedagogical quality improved by nearly 25%, increasing the outright approval rate by expert reviewers from 76% to 95%. Across in-platform tasks and intermediate quizzes, students receiving AI tutoring performed similarly to those paired with human tutors. Just as importantly, AI tutoring promoted active thinking rather than shortcuts: following a pedagogical prompt we provided, Gemini guided students instead of handing them answers in nearly 99% of sessions, and students worked through the math themselves in more than 85% of their chats.

While the use of AI tutoring led to clear gains on daily classroom tasks and quizzes, these gains didn’t show up on STAR standardized test scores over the same trial period. After exploring more, we believe this can be attributed to step-by-step tutoring taking more time per question than using simple hints. Students in the trial therefore solved fewer total problems per session (averaging about 14 with AI tutoring versus 19 with static hints). Over 10 weeks, that lower volume meant students covered less overall curriculum material—even as their pacing and understanding improved—indicating the trial length wasn't long enough to cover the broad range of topics on the STAR test. To examine this trend further, we are exploring follow-up trials across a full academic year while also expanding our metrics to better understand what drives meaningful learning and eventual outcomes.

You can find more details in our full technical report.

Italy: Creating a more active classroom

Following our initial pilot in Northern Italy, we worked with the Salesians of Don Bosco school network and the Pontifical Salesian University in Rome on a yearlong study across 31 schools. Together, we learned from Primary, Secondary and Vocational educators across 1,600 teachers (representing over 24,500 students ages 13-18) by collecting classroom activities and self reports on lesson planning both with and without Gemini for Education to understand how AI supports classroom dynamics, student engagement, and teacher wellbeing.

The findings show that AI is most effective when educators remain at the center of the classroom and learning. When educators used Gemini to co-design lessons, they reported feeling more creative than usual in their teaching and planning (79% with Gemini vs. 30% without Gemini) — a shift that helped transform classroom dynamics. Traditional front of the classroom lectures dropped by 38%, making way for workshops, group activities and peer discussions that nearly tripled student-led collaborative learning. In turn, students responded positively to the collaborative environment and active lessons created by their teachers. In lessons teachers co-designed with Gemini, more students actively participated in class (with student reported engagement rising from 77% to 84%) while debating diverse viewpoints more often and taking greater ownership of their learning.

Beyond improving classroom dynamics, the study showed a meaningful impact on teacher wellbeing. Educators often carry the heavy burden of relying solely on their own energy to keep a room engaged but in lessons co-planned with Gemini, that reliance dropped by 66%. Instead, lessons where the activity design itself drove engagement more than doubled (from 23.2% to 52.2%), carrying the momentum of the class and relieving some of that daily pressure of keeping students engaged.

Even on days with tight prep time, having AI as a thought partner to adapt materials gave educators the support they needed to focus on what matters most: mentoring and connecting with their students. More details about the implementation and study can be found in the Don Bosco CNOS-FAP Foundation implementation report.

entries.title: Partnering with Singapore to bring frontier AI to public health
entries.summary: Speakers on stage at the Google for Health Singapore Summit.
entries.content:
We're deepening our partnership with Singapore to deploy frontier AI across the nation’s healthcare system. The primary goals of the new collaboration, announced at the Google for Health Summit in Singapore, are to accelerate scientific discoveries, transform clinical care delivery, and empower Singaporeans with proactive health tools.

Working closely with local researchers, clinicians, and public agencies, we share a vision of using technology where it will have the greatest impact: driving medical breakthroughs, helping frontline workers focus on patient care, giving people better ways to manage their health, and expanding preventive care across the community.

Here is a look at how this work is coming to life across Singapore.

Accelerating scientific breakthroughs and local research

We’re establishing a Google Research hub in Singapore composed of local research scientists and software engineers. The group will focus on driving advancements in foundational AI models to accelerate scientific breakthroughs. It will also partner with academic institutions, such as the National University of Singapore and Nanyang Technological University, to help nurture future scientific leaders and provide targeted research support.

Google Research will also scale its existing health research initiatives in Singapore. This includes bringing open models like MedGemma to frontline care settings to enable the development of secure, customized solutions while maintaining full data sovereignty.

To advance scientific research, Google.org and Google DeepMind are contributing $7 million to the Philanthropy Asia Alliance’s Health for Human Potential Coalition. This includes $1 million for PathGen, an AI platform that uses Google technology to help countries detect disease threats faster and share data for public health intelligence while protecting in-country data sovereignty.

Supporting clinicians and advancing population-scale health

To support frontline care, Google DeepMind is working with the National University Health System to evaluate our AI co-clinician tool that helps clinicians quickly synthesize information from medical guidelines and literature, and assist doctors with clinical queries as they care for patients.

Additionally, Google Cloud is partnering with NHG Health on a population health program that uses AI-driven predictive insights to forecast health risks, such as chronic conditions, across sub-populations. These insights feed directly into an AI health coach on the NHG HealthBot, using Google’s Gemini Enterprise for Customer Experience platform, to deliver personalized lifestyle guidance and preventative care reminders to residents.

Reinforcing commitments to public health

True impact in healthcare requires advanced technology. It also relies on a health system's ability to integrate AI responsibly, govern it safely, and translate it into human-centered care.

As countries around the world face shared challenges like an aging population and navigating the shift toward personalized and preventive care, pairing our technical expertise with Singapore’s world-class healthcare institutions will help build a future-ready system that serves as a blueprint for scaling AI safely for public good.

entries.title: Ads in AI Mode expand to new markets.
entries.summary: Google is expanding AI Mode ads to 10 new countries, including Canada and India. See how these relevant sponsored results improve your search experience.
entries.content:
We’re bringing ads in AI Mode to new countries.

As AI transforms how people search, queries are becoming increasingly conversational. In AI Mode, queries are, on average, three times longer than traditional searches. 1 AI helps us better understand what people are looking for, allowing us to connect them to the businesses and services that best match their needs.

Our research shows that people are comfortable with ads in AI Mode and find them highly relevant. In fact, click-through rates are already similar between sponsored and organic product list items within AI Mode. 2

Now we're scaling ads in AI Mode in Australia, Canada, India, Kenya, Malaysia, New Zealand, Nigeria, Pakistan, the Philippines, and Singapore. In Q4 2026, we plan to expand to additional locales, including Brazil, Mexico, and the United Kingdom.

To allow ads in follow-up queries in AI Mode, we are launching multiturn ads in the U.S.

Ads will be clearly labeled as “Sponsored.” We’ll continue testing new formats to ensure ads remain helpful and relevant.

Learn more here.

entries.title: Q3 2026 earnings call: Remarks from our CEO
entries.summary: Read Sundar Pichai’s remarks during Alphabet’s Q3 2026 earnings call.
entries.content:
Q3 was a strong quarter for Alphabet. Our deep, full-stack approach is driving momentum across the business, with many opportunities ahead.

Alphabet revenues grew 25% year-over-year. We’re now at a half-trillion-dollar annual run rate — that’s remarkable growth.

Search has strong momentum. Our AI investments are driving increased usage and overall query growth, including commercial queries. In fact, our year-over-year query growth rate is the highest it’s been in the last five years.

Google Cloud revenues grew 103%. Our AI infrastructure and solutions are the major drivers for Cloud growth and our customers see us as the leading provider here, so there’s huge demand. We are working hard to bring more capacity online to meet this long-term demand. At the same time, we’re seeing strong demand for our TPU systems across a wide range of customers, and we expect that to continue as we scale.

On our AI models: Customers are using our models more than ever. Our first-party model APIs are now processing nearly 32 billion tokens per minute — 40% more than last quarter and more than four times what we processed a year ago. And with Gemini 4 Argon and now Carbon, which we announced today, we’re excited to be leading at the frontier.

The Gemini app is now at one billion users and is the fastest-growing product in Google’s history.

Lastly, we’ve surpassed 150 million YouTube Music and Premium subscribers globally, including trials.

Today, I'll talk more about our AI progress, our global consumer platforms led by Search and YouTube, then our long-term bets.

AI progress

Starting with AI, highlighted by our Gemini 4 series of frontier models.

We’re seeing strong demand and usage for Argon, which we launched two weeks ago. In fact, on our developer platforms, usage in the first week ramped up three-and-a-half times faster than Gemini 3, even with capacity constraints.

Argon is proving to do really well in areas like finance, legal, cybersecurity, and science. Developers and Cloud customers are already using it for things like untangling legacy codebases, accelerating scientific research, robotics, discovering product improvements, and domain-specific tasks requiring in-depth reasoning. And at Google, just in the last few weeks, teams across Chrome, Ads, and Search have used Argon to write and optimize code much faster, shipping 35% more code with 30% fewer errors.

Argon is just the start of the Gemini 4 series. Today, we announced Carbon. It’s our strongest frontier model, with state-of-the-art cybersecurity and long horizon capabilities. It ranks #1 on the recently updated Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index at 59.

Carbon outperforms Argon across almost every domain, like full-stack web development, multimodal understanding, complex knowledge work, and scientific reasoning.

We're rolling Carbon out first to a subset of trusted cyber defenders before we expand access, and it's being tested by the U.S. government.

Beyond our Gemini 4 series, yesterday we announced Genie 4, our most advanced world model yet that simulates safe, realistic, interactive worlds with native audio in real time. This is an important building block for training robots and agents.

This rapid progress underscores our incredible model momentum. We’re at the point where AI is helping us increase our training and launch velocity. I would expect the next 12 months to see continued acceleration because of RSI. We have more models coming soon, including more efficient versions to help developers optimize for speed and cost and to deploy across our billions of users.

Search

Search is bringing the benefits of AI to more people than any other product in the world. Just like our shift to mobile over a decade ago, we are focused on building the best Search user experience, followed by monetization.

We are building one seamless experience across AI Overviews, AI Mode, and traditional Search. And people are using our AI features more, searching in entirely new ways. Their queries are longer, personalized, and multimodal. Queries in AI Mode are on average three times longer than traditional searches, and one in five AI Mode searches globally use voice, images, or documents. We’ve now crossed over 50 billion visual searches per month.

Agentic experiences

One area I’m excited about is helping people get things done, be it booking reservations, filling in forms, scheduling appointments, or making purchases. As AI becomes more personal and starts taking action for people and businesses, trust and security matter more than ever. People already put their trust in Google to get things done in their daily lives, and our leadership here remains an important differentiator.

We focused first on getting these agentic experiences right with the Gemini agent for enterprise because the bar for security, safety, and governance is extremely high.

As a next step, we’re bringing these features to Search. And also, of course, to our billion users on the Gemini app. People are already using the Gemini app to do more than ask questions; they’re using it to do things, including complex, multi-step agentic queries. Our Gemini 4 series has been a really big step forward here, and has already been handling these complex tasks really well.

Agents will operate as a unifying layer across our products, so you’ll see us extend these agentic experiences beyond Search and the Gemini app to Chrome, Android, and our Workspace products as well.

YouTube

On to YouTube, which continues to lead in the living room as the number-one streaming platform in the U.S. in terms of watch time. It’s also seeing good subscriber growth, as I mentioned.

At Made on YouTube last month, we announced more than 30 products and features for creators and viewers. One great example is custom feeds, where you can simply pick a topic you love and get a tailored video home feed based on that topic.

Other Bets

On to our long-term bets. Waymo is on a great trajectory. We’ve now driven more than 300 million fully autonomous miles. Waymo now operates in 15 major U.S. cities and just recently opened up service to the public in San Antonio, San Diego, and Tampa, with planned expansions into Canada, Germany, Singapore, and Spain.

We’re also seeing strong progress across our other long-term initiatives. Isomorphic is using Argon to support drug design research. We demonstrated “magic state cultivation” for the first time in quantum computing, and launched our TPUs into space with Project Suncatcher.

So it’s been a busy quarter and there’s much more to come. I want to thank our employees for their work this quarter.
